nodes.label: FxDigitalBarrierOptionData Trade Type
nodes.rationale: Combines a single continuously-monitored American barrier (as in FxTouchOption) with a strike test at expiry (Call/Put), paying a fixed cash amount only if both the barrier condition and the in/out-of-the-money condition are satisfied.

nodes.label: FXIndexDailyLows/FXIndexDailyHighs Intraday Barrier Monitoring
nodes.rationale: If not explicitly given, ORE derives the daily-low/high index name by appending _LOW/_HIGH to the FXIndex source, falling back to the plain FXIndex fixings if none are available, so a single FXIndex reference can drive both a check-date-close and an intraday-extreme barrier test.

nodes.label: FxDigitalOptionData Trade Type
nodes.rationale: A pure cash-or-nothing FX digital with no barrier component: the fixed PayoffAmount is paid solely based on whether the FX rate at expiry is above (Call) or below (Put) the Strike.

nodes.label: FxDoubleBarrierOptionData Trade Type
nodes.rationale: European-exercise vanilla FX option existence gated by two continuously-monitored (American) barrier levels; once knocked in, a knock-in option behaves as a Vanilla FX Option for the rest of its life.

nodes.label: Put/Call Bought-Sold Currency Switch Convention
nodes.rationale: Put options do not need the barrier levels re-quoted: the Bought/Sold currencies and amounts are logically swapped relative to the Call representation, but the barrier level stays quoted as SoldCurrency per unit BoughtCurrency in the original (Call) orientation.

nodes.label: FxDoubleTouchOptionData Trade Type
nodes.rationale: Pays a fixed cash amount if the FX rate has hit either of two barrier levels (KnockIn) or hit neither (KnockOut) under continuous monitoring; no rebates are supported and OptionType is inferred/omitted.

nodes.label: PayOffAtExpiry Restriction (Double Touch)
nodes.rationale: Currently only payoff-at-expiry (true) is supported for both KnockOut and KnockIn double-touch barriers, unlike the single-barrier FxTouchOption which documents (but restricts) a payoff-at-hit concept.

nodes.label: FxEuropeanBarrierOptionData Trade Type
nodes.rationale: The underlying FX rate is checked against a single barrier only at expiry (European/discrete monitoring) rather than continuously, distinguishing it from the American-barrier FxBarrierOption and FxDoubleBarrierOption.

nodes.label: Settlement (Cash/Physical) and PaymentData
nodes.rationale: An optional PaymentData node under OptionData defers the settlement date of the option payoff away from the exercise date, independent of whether settlement is Cash or Physical.

nodes.label: FxKIKOBarrierOptionData Trade Type
nodes.rationale: European-exercise option with both a continuously-monitored knock-out and knock-in barrier: once the knock-in barrier is touched the trade becomes a single American-barrier knock-out trade, exercisable only if the knock-out barrier is never touched and the knock-in barrier is touched at least once.

nodes.label: Barriers Node (Paired KnockIn + KnockOut BarrierData)
nodes.rationale: Exactly two BarrierData blocks are required inside the Barriers node, one of type UpAndIn/DownAndIn and one of UpAndOut/DownAndOut; unlike most FX barrier trades, FxKIKOBarrierOptions do not currently support rebates.

nodes.label: FxTouchOptionData Trade Type
nodes.rationale: One Touch (UpAndIn/DownAndIn) or No Touch (UpAndOut/DownAndOut) cash payoff under continuous monitoring; no rebates are supported, and the GenericBarrierOption trade type can be used to replicate a payoff-at-hit variant if required.

nodes.label: OptionType Inferred from Barrier Direction
nodes.rationale: The OptionType sub-node is not required for FxTouchOption: it is inferred from the BarrierData Type (Call for an Up barrier, Put for a Down barrier), and if the option pays at hit, PaymentData must be rules-based with RelativeTo set to Exercise.

nodes.label: FX Accumulator (Scripted Trade)
nodes.rationale: Represented as a ScriptedTrade referencing the 'Accumulator' script rather than a dedicated trade type; the FX-specific instantiation reuses the same generic script logic as the equity/commodity accumulators, differing only in the underlying Index and PayCcy data bindings.

nodes.label: Range Leverage Bounds and KnockOutLevel/GuaranteedFixings
nodes.rationale: RangeUpperBounds/RangeLowerBounds/RangeLeverages define a piecewise leverage schedule applied to each fixing's accumulated amount, while GuaranteedFixings lets the first n fixings continue to accrue even after the KnockOutLevel barrier has been breached.

nodes.label: FxForwardData Trade Type
nodes.rationale: The FX rate 'fixes' at ValueDate; before that date the contract value fluctuates with market FX rates, and Non-Deliverable Forwards are represented simply via Cash settlement rather than a distinct trade type.

nodes.label: SettlementData (Cash Settlement Rules)
nodes.rationale: When settlement is Cash and the payment date is after the value date, an FXIndex fixing is required; the Rules sub-node (PaymentLag/PaymentCalendar/PaymentConvention) derives the payment date from the value date, defaulting to the referenced FX index's own convention fields when omitted.

nodes.label: FxAverageForwardData Trade Type
nodes.rationale: A distinct trade type documented in the same file: its payoff is driven by an arithmetic average of FX fixings over ObservationDates rather than a single fixing, converting a ReferenceNotional at the average rate against a fixed SettlementNotional.

nodes.label: FXOptionData Trade Type
nodes.rationale: Supports both European and American exercise; for Put options the Bought/Sold currencies and amounts are logically switched relative to the Call representation, mirroring the convention used across the FX barrier trade types.

nodes.label: Delta-Derived Strike (vs SoldAmount)
nodes.rationale: When Delta is given the strike is derived from it as of the valuation date and SoldAmount is ignored; because the delta-to-strike conversion is revalued daily against market data, a seasoned trade cannot be entered with a fixed historical strike derived from Delta.

nodes.label: AutomaticExercise (Past-Expiry Outstanding Cashflow)
nodes.rationale: Used when the FXOption expiry date is on or before the valuation date but the payment date is still in the future: the FX fixing on the expiry date is used to automatically determine whether the option was exercised and thus the outstanding payoff amount.

nodes.label: FXSwapData Trade Type
nodes.rationale: Contains no trade-component sub-nodes at all: near-date and far-date bought/sold currencies and amounts are given as flat sibling elements rather than nested OptionData/LegData structures.

nodes.label: FxVarianceSwapData Trade Type
nodes.rationale: Only vanilla FX variance swaps are covered by this dedicated trade type; exotic variance swaps are instead built via the generic ScriptedTrade framework.

nodes.label: MomentType (Volatility vs Variance Strike Convention)
nodes.rationale: The Strike element is always quoted as a volatility regardless of MomentType; MomentType only flags whether the swap is contractually struck in volatility or variance terms, decoupling quotation convention from contractual moment type.

nodes.label: Generic Barrier Option (Fx/Equity/Commodity)
nodes.rationale: A single flexible schema (FxGenericBarrierOptionData / EquityGenericBarrierOptionData / CommodityGenericBarrierOptionData) supports one or multiple underlyings, multiple named payoff types, and combinable American plus Transatlantic barriers, generalizing the narrower single-purpose FX/Equity barrier trade types.

nodes.label: Barriers Node (ScheduleData + Multiple BarrierData + KikoType)
nodes.rationale: Supports an arbitrary sequence of BarrierData blocks (not just one or two as in the narrower FX barrier trades) each with independent Rebate/RebateCurrency/RebatePayTime/StrictComparison, with KikoType (KoAlways/KoBeforeKi/KoAfterKi) required only when both KI and KO barriers are present.

nodes.label: TransatlanticBarrier (Additional Expiry-Only Barrier Check)
nodes.rationale: An additional barrier checked only at option expiry on top of the American barriers in the Barriers node; its rebate is paid only if there was no knock-out from the American barriers and no payoff from the Transatlantic barrier itself.

nodes.label: PayoffType (Vanilla / AssetOrNothing / CashOrNothing)
nodes.rationale: PayoffType selects which of three payoff formulas is used (max(0,S-K)/max(0,K-S) for Vanilla, S for AssetOrNothing, a fixed Amount for CashOrNothing), each of which is paid in PayCurrency and can be quanto if PayCurrency differs from the underlying's natural currency.

nodes.label: Generic Scripted Products (Overview)
nodes.rationale: Explains that several 'classic-looking' ORE trade types (double digital option through TaRF) are internally represented as Scripted Trades wrapped so their input XML still resembles non-scripted ORE trade data, bridging the flexible payoff-scripting engine and the fixed per-trade-type schema documentation.

nodes.label: IndexCreditDefaultSwapData Trade Type
nodes.rationale: The premium LegData must be a Fixed leg whose Payer flag determines whether the trade is bought or sold protection; an optional BasketData sub-node overrides the standard index constituents derived from CreditCurveId for bespoke, non-standard indices.

nodes.label: Unfactored vs Trade-Date vs Current (Factored) Notional
nodes.rationale: The fixed leg notional in the XML is always the 'unfactored' (pre-default) notional; this is distinct from the trade-date notional (reduced by defaults since series inception up to the trade date) and the current/factored notional (further reduced up to the valuation date), both computed internally by ORE.

nodes.label: SettlesAccrual / ProtectionPaymentTime / RebatesAccrual
nodes.rationale: ProtectionPaymentTime (atDefault/atPeriodEnd/atMaturity) overrides the deprecated PaysAtDefaultTime boolean; RebatesAccrual models the protection seller paying accrued current coupon at contract start, with the rebate date computed as two days after protection start rather than being explicitly given.

nodes.label: IndexCreditDefaultSwapOptionData Trade Type
nodes.rationale: An option to enter into an index CDS at a specified strike spread or price; only European exercise and payoff-at-exercise (PayOffAtExpiry=false) are supported, and the underlying IndexCreditDefaultSwapData's TradeDate/ProtectionStart are recommended to be left blank so ORE can derive them correctly from the option's ExerciseDate.

nodes.label: IndexTerm (Volatility Surface Selector)
nodes.rationale: When populated, IndexTerm appends a -[IndexTerm] suffix to the CreditCurveId to look up a term-specific CDS volatility surface (e.g. CDXHYS34V1-5Y vs CDXHYS34V1-10Y), letting different terms of the same index series use distinct volatility structures; if omitted it is derived from the underlying schedule's start/end dates.

nodes.label: Strike/StrikeType Effective Resolution Table
nodes.rationale: A documented lookup table resolves the effective Strike and StrikeType from the combination of the given Strike, StrikeType and the underlying IndexCDS's UpfrontFee, disallowing certain combinations outright (e.g. a non-zero UpfrontFee together with an explicit Spread strike).

nodes.label: FrontEndProtectionStartDate / TradeDate Default Handling
nodes.rationale: TradeDate governs whether pre-auction-date defaulted notional counts as outstanding, while FrontEndProtectionStartDate (defaulting to TradeDate) governs whether a defaulted name contributes to the realised front-end protection amount; both must be populated accurately when defaults occurred in the underlying index or valuation may be inaccurate.

nodes.label: CdoData (Index Tranche / Synthetic CDO) Trade Type
nodes.rationale: Documents the CdoData block used for a tranche on a credit index: a Qualifier references the base correlation curve, and the LegData/BasketData sub-structure mirrors that of a plain Index Credit Default Swap but scoped to the tranche's initial notional.

nodes.label: AttachmentPoint / DetachmentPoint (Tranche Loss Bounds)
nodes.rationale: AttachmentPoint and DetachmentPoint, expressed as fractions of the basket notional, delimit the loss layer over which the tranche's protection applies, the defining feature that turns a basket/index CDS into a synthetic CDO tranche.

nodes.label: Trade Data (Portfolio XML Introduction)
nodes.rationale: Establishes the shared XML skeleton (Portfolio > Trade > Envelope + trade-specific data node) that every per-trade-type schema documented elsewhere in tradedata/*.tex builds upon.

nodes.label: Envelope Node (Common Trade Wrapper Fields)
nodes.rationale: Every trade, regardless of TradeType, carries the same Envelope elements (CounterParty, NettingSetId, PortfolioIds, AdditionalFields) ahead of the trade-type-specific data node, providing the uniform hook point used by NettingSetDetails as an alternative to a plain NettingSetId.

nodes.label: KnockOutSwapData Trade Type
nodes.rationale: A vanilla fixed-vs-float IRS that terminates entirely when the floating index fixing crosses a barrier level; requires exactly one Fixed and one Floating LegData plus a single BarrierData node.

nodes.label: BarrierStartDate (Floating Fixing Monitoring Window)
nodes.rationale: The barrier is only monitored on floating-leg fixing dates on or after BarrierStartDate, letting a swap have an initial guaranteed (non-knockable) period before barrier surveillance begins.

nodes.label: NettingSetDetails Node
nodes.rationale: An alternative to a bare NettingSetId inside the trade Envelope: bundles NettingSetId with four optional qualifiers so netting sets can be disambiguated beyond a single ID string, e.g. across multiple CSAs/legal agreements sharing the same counterparty.

nodes.label: AgreementType/CallType/InitialMarginType/LegalEntityId Sub-nodes
nodes.rationale: All four qualifier sub-nodes accept any alphanumeric string (including underscores), giving free-form extensibility rather than a fixed enumeration, so netting set identity can be extended arbitrarily to match a firm's internal collateral/legal taxonomy.
